name: Two rivers

sections.name: Two rivers: Bass river
sections.why: The drums and your bass, no melody.

sections.name: Two rivers: Wood river
sections.why: No bass: the drops and the marimba, a rim in sevens against the four.

sections.name: Two rivers: Bass river, rolling
sections.why: Your line's notes on the rolling-threes rhythm: the same notes, a new way of walking.

sections.name: Two rivers: Where they meet
sections.why: Bass and marimba together for the first time, on E minor 7 to F major 7; the kick broken.

sections.name: Two rivers: Bass river
sections.why: The theme again, as it was.

sections.name: Two rivers: Wood river, no kick
sections.why: The kick drops out; the drops developed over four bars.

sections.name: Two rivers: The sea
sections.why: Both rivers at once, strings under them.

why: A rondo (A B A C A B, then the sea): the bass and the wood take turns, never together until they meet. The bass's river on D minor, the wood's on the A pedal, and where they meet a darker turn, a semitone up and back.
